name: Goretek MaintenanceRun Zip Cargo Trouser
description: Loose-fit work trousers in faded brown canvas with eight externally visible maintenance zips — two at each major joint zone, sized for standard and wide-body chrome housings. The zips are heavy brass-tooth in an era of hidden fasteners, and they're meant to be seen: this is a garment built for someone who needs access fast. Knees are double-layered canvas. Hem is adjustable with a snap-tab for different leg configurations.
functionality: Eight maintenance zips positioned at standard chrome joint access zones. Adjustable snap-tab hem for variable leg geometry.
what_it_says: You do real work and your clothes are tools, not statements.
story_hooks: A tech who wears these keeps a small unauthorized tool set in the zip pockets — items that never show on a standard pat-down.
The zipper placement matches a specific corponation's proprietary chrome housing spec; someone is wondering who designed this pattern and why.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian work trouser with a distinctly mechanical aesthetic. The loose, relaxed silhouette hangs straight from hip to ankle with deliberate room through the thigh and calf for movement and chrome housing accommodation. Eight prominent brass-tooth zips create a vertical emphasis pattern down the legs, reading as functional armor rather than fashion. The overall impression is working-class pragmatism with visible infrastructure.
physical_description.fit: Loose and spacious throughout. Cut generously through the hip and thigh to accommodate augmented limbs and standard-width chrome housings. Straight leg with no taper. Inseam adjustability suggests wear across multiple body configurations.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-weight canvas in faded brown — likely a treated synthetic-organic blend optimized for durability and stain resistance in industrial environments.
physical_description.texture: Coarse, slightly stiff canvas with visible weave. Double-layered at knee zones for reinforcement. Brass zips have a granular, oxidized patina typical of frequent use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded medium-brown canvas as primary color. Brass zips provide warm metallic accents with natural oxidation variation. Possible oil stains or discoloration in high-use areas.
physical_description.closures: Eight external brass-tooth zips positioned at ankle (2), knee (2), mid-thigh (2), and hip/groin (2) zones. Snap-tab hem adjustment at cuffs. Likely a magnetic snap or friction-fit waistband.
distinctive_features: Eight prominently displayed brass-tooth zips in deliberate joint-zone placement
Snap-tab adjustable hem for prosthetic/chrome leg length variation
Oversized cut designed to accommodate wide-body augmentations
Heavy brass hardware resisting minimalist design trends
Likely reinforced seams and gussets in stress zones
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional workwear. High-quality construction and specialized engineering signal investment and legitimacy, but the utilitarian aesthetic and lack of luxury materials place it firmly in working-class territory.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by maintenance technicians, field engineers, industrial workers, and augmentation specialists who need rapid access to joint zones for repair or adjustment. The visible zips communicate competence and honesty — this person works on machines, including their own body.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered. Canvas shows fading and possible staining. Zips function smoothly despite visible patina. Hems may show fraying at adjustable snap points. Knees show creasing and minor wear spots from kneeling.
